subject: Math
prompt:
$$3 t + 10 = 25$$

A plant had a height of $10$ inches when it was first measured. The equation shown can be used to find the number of months $t$ it took the plant to reach a height of $25$ inches. Which of the following is the best interpretation of the number $3$ in this context?

choices.A: The number of months it took the plant to triple its height
choices.B: The average number of inches that the plant grew per month
choices.C: The average number of months it takes similar plants to grow $25$ inches
choices.D: The height, in inches, of the plant when the plant was $1$ month old

explanation: Choice B is correct. The height of the plant at a given time equals its initial height plus the total growth. In the given equation, $25$ represents the height at the later time and $10$ represents the initial height, so $3t$ represents the total number of inches the plant grew over $t$ months. Since $t$ is the number of months, the coefficient $3$ represents the average number of inches the plant grew each month.
